chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The fasting for the expiation of the oath in Dhihar is two consecutive months, and consecutiveness is that he fasts one month and fasts from the other month some days or a part of it. So if something occurs to him that causes him to break his fast, he breaks it, then he makes up for what remains upon him. And if he fasts one month, then something occurs to him, so he breaks before he fasts anything from the other month, so he has not maintained consecutiveness, he must repeat the entire fasting.

key_terms.الظِّهَارِ: Dhihar (a form of divorce in pre-Islamic and early Islamic law)
key_terms.يُفْطَرُ فِيهِ: That which causes breaking of the fast

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for maintaining consecutive fasting for Dhihar expiation if one breaks their fast?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential nuance of 'consecutive' (mutatabi') fasting for Dhihar expiation, distinguishing between permissible interruptions that preserve the count and those that reset it. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing strict obligation with practical ease, ensuring the expiation is fulfilled without undue hardship. The ruling underscores the importance of intention and continuity in ritual acts, a key theme in Usul al-Fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Fasting as an expiation for the oath regarding the Zihaar is of two consecutive months, and the ‘consecutive’ is that he Fasts a month and Fasts from the other month a few days, or something from it. So if something presents itself to him to break in it, he breaks. Then he makes up for what remains upon him. And if he Fasts a month, then something presents itself to him, so he breaks before he Fasts anything from the other (month), so he has not followed it. He has to repeat the Fasts, all of it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

In fasting, as expiation for an oath in the case of Zihar which is two consecutive months of fasting, consecutive order is established by fasting one whole month and certain days of the next month or something thereof. Thereafter if something occurs to him he may eat and then carryout Qada’ (compensatory fast) of what remains of the two months. If one fasts for one month only, then something occurs before fasting even one day of the second month, because of which one stops fasting, consecutive order becomes invalid; thus one is required to start all over again.’”
